description.value: Task-fMRI comparison of reward anticipation in cigarette smokers and nonsmokers, testing whether striatal responses to immediate versus equally preferred delayed rewards differ between groups.

Cross-sectional observational comparison of smokers and nonsmokers. Both groups performed the same immediate/delayed reward task. Smokers were not required to abstain and were invited to smoke before scanning. A subset completed a post-task delay-discounting reassessment.

name.value: spatial working memory (SWM) and vigilance paradigm

description.value: Eighteen 20-second blocks alternating SWM and vigilance, with fixation rest at the beginning, middle, and end. Stimuli appeared for 1,000 ms with 1,000-ms interstimulus intervals; total duration 7 minutes 48 seconds.
Abstract line drawings appear in one of eight locations; press a button when a design repeats a location already occupied in that block. On average three of ten trials repeat, with repeats 2-back.
The same stimuli and locations are presented, but a dot appears above figures on 30% of trials; press a button when a dot appears. Controls simple motor and attention processes.
Rest with a fixation cross in the center of the screen at the beginning, middle, and end.

description.value: Psychiatric diagnoses from youth and parent reports; administered to parents by different interviewers to corroborate adolescent reports.

Eleven clusters from the SWM-versus-vigilance single-sample t-test; the largest was divided into nine smaller ROIs using regional proximity, structure–function correlates, and activation direction. Table 3 lists 15 foci, including the divided largest cluster. Participant-average activation was converted to z-scores.
